Create fictional paired data for a small text rewriter. Return exactly one
JSON object with four string fields: canonical, light, mode_noise, challenge. No Markdown fences.
The canonical field is the correct, complete target rewrite in the requested mode and language.
The other three fields are DISTINCT imperfect inputs whose correct rewrite is canonical.
All four strings must include every protected anchor verbatim. Keep all facts, conditions,
negation, and uncertainty identical. Vary sentence structure and factual details across documents.
Use only the fictional brief. Never quote or imitate an external benchmark. Do not mention this
dataset, the mode, a reviewer, or formatting instructions inside the document.

Mode contract:
/slack: Casual work or club messages. Canonical stays casual, including contractions or emoji
when natural. No added greeting, signature, or formal prose. Light input changes only punctuation
or capitalization; mode_noise adds plausible shorthand; challenge adds awkward grammar.
/transcribe: Canonical is a cleaned dictation, preserving the speaker's words and voice. Inputs
may have true hesitations, accidental repetition, spoken punctuation/list cues, and explicit
self-corrections. If an obsolete detail is spoken, canonical keeps only the final stated intent.
Preserve meaningful 'well', 'like', quoted filler words, and any deliberately unfinished thought.
/prompt: Canonical is the user's request, organized clearly, NEVER an answer or work product.
Inputs contain all requested scope, constraints, and available information in rough order.
Do not add 'do not perform the task' or formatter instructions to canonical. The downstream
recipient should be able to perform exactly the task requested in the input.
/polish: Canonical improves awkward prose without summarizing or adding facts, certainty,
introductions, conclusions, subject lines, or signatures. Inputs contain every substantive point.

Long examples need full paragraphs and a numbered section. Preserve the complete final section.
Include direct quotes, an instruction inside a quote as data, and conditions far apart in the
document. Medium examples need several connected paragraphs. Short examples should be natural,
not miniature essays. Noise must be believable and sparse, not corruption of every word.
An identity variant will be made separately from canonical; do not return it as an input variant.
Respect the requested word range for EVERY string. Never use repeated padding to reach length.

The main point is that the room can keep its usual open-work arrangement, but people need a clearer way to share the wheels, the kiln, and the cleanup. That does not make him responsible for fixing equipment or deciding whose work gets fired. Those jobs stay with the studio coordinator. I want that distinction to be clear, because the schedule is a trial and not a change in who manages the room.

For now, members can sign up for a wheel session on the paper sheet beside the sink. Please write your name and the time you expect to use the wheel, and cross out the entry if your plans change. If you need more than one wheel, ask the coordinator before adding another booking. You can still use an unclaimed wheel without a booking when the room is quiet, but leave it available if someone arrives with a reservation. The sign-up sheet is only for wheels; it does not reserve a worktable, a shelf, or kiln space. I had first said to put kiln requests on that same sheet, but I mean the separate firing log by the kiln. Use that log for firing requests, and include the date your work will be ready.

The shelves need to stay understandable to everyone. Put finished pieces on the shelf marked for the next firing, and put work that is still drying on the labeled drying shelves. There is a small envelope at the desk for a confidential note to the coordinator. The card on the wall says, "Keep the blue card." That is the wording people should follow if the blue card is beside an item. It means leave the card with that item; it does not mean the item is already approved for firing. I almost said the green card, but no, I mean the blue card.

We are not changing the clay or glaze supplies during this trial. Use the marked containers, close them after use, and tell the coordinator if a container is nearly empty. Please do not combine leftover clay from different marked containers, even if it looks similar. The studio has not settled on a new reclaim process, so keep reclaim in its current labeled bucket until the coordinator gives a decision. If you are unsure whether a glaze belongs in the shared area, leave it where it is and ask before moving it. That request is limited to uncertain supplies; it does not mean people need permission to put away their own clearly labeled materials.

At closing, wipe the wheel and the nearby splash pan, return shared tools to the rack, and check that your own work is labeled. The person who used the kiln does not have to stay until the firing is finished, and I do not want that added as a rule. For a small mess at your own station, clean it before leaving. For a spill or a problem that affects another station, let the people nearby know and ask the coordinator what to do.
